display.title: Sefiras HaOmer: Respect for Each Other and the Gift of Time
display.summary_short: Why we avoid music during Sefirah, how to practice respect and peace, and why counting the Omer teaches us never to waste the precious gift of time.
display.summary_long: A Sefirah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show in two parts. First, Uncle Yossi explains that we do not listen to music during Sefirah because Rabbi Akiva's many students died in a plague for failing to show each other respect. He describes respect for parents, teachers and friends, looking for the good in others, avoiding quarrels and pursuing peace, and says that unity and setting a good example are the answer to 'Ad mosai, how long until Moshiach?'. Second, he teaches that counting the Omer shows how precious every day is: each day's number is higher than the last, so today must be better than yesterday. A story about a girl named Miriam, who keeps crying over a lost dime even after her mother gives her more, shows that we cannot get lost time back and must use the time we are given well. Time is like a treasure of jewels to be counted, and using it for Torah and mitzvos brings long life, as the Shema promises.
display.lesson: Respect one another, and treasure each day: make it better than the one before and never waste the gift of time.
